cohort: Nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies who delivered at a large academic hospital between April and July of 2019 or 2020.
finding: There was a statistically significant decrease in cesarean delivery rates during the COVID-19 pandemic compared to the same period one year prior, primarily due to an increase in the rate of women attempting a trial of labor.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean delivery during labor was unchanged between the two groups, but more women attempted a trial of labor during the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to a decrease in the proportion of cesarean deliveries without a trial of labor.
gest_age: median gestational age at delivery was similar between groups
